cards.note: Spoken: «kat» for «di» (at, in). Standard first: di (Ch2). Ada kedai mamak kat depan pejabat.
Spoken: «kan» = «right?», «isn't it?» (a confirmation particle). It is not the suffix -kan (Ch12). You will hear it; saying it is optional. Recognise only.

cards.gloss_en: softening or emphasis particle (spoken; meaning depends on tone)
cards.gloss_ja: 語調を調整する助詞（話し言葉・文脈による）
cards.note: Spoken: «lah» softens or stresses what is said; the meaning depends on the tone, so it has no one-word translation. You will hear it; saying it is optional. Recognise only.

cards.gloss_en: To invite along; to ask someone to come (informal)
cards.note: To invite someone along, informally: Saya ajak encik. Compare jom (Ch2) and jemput (Dunia, Ch9): the tone differs; they are not the same word in short form.
To be willing, glad to (polite). We use it to ask the other person, not about ourselves: Sudikah encik datang?
Free, not busy: Hari Sabtu saya tidak lapang.
To agree. The standard form; the spoken partner is «set!» (below). Learn it as a whole word.

cards.gloss_en: to decline, to refuse (also to push)
cards.note: meN- + tolak (Ch9). The t drops: menolak. A new sense of tolak (push): to decline, to refuse. Saya segan untuk menolak jemputan puan.
cadang + -an: a suggestion. Itu cadangan yang bagus.

cards.gloss_ja: 遠慮する・気が引ける
cards.note: Hesitant, shy about doing something: Saya segan untuk menolak jemputan puan.
sayang + -nya: what a pity. Sayangnya hari Sabtu saya tidak lapang.
malang + -nya: unfortunately. Malangnya saya ada mesyuarat.
Another time: lain (Ch6) + kali (Ch3). A fixed phrase: Lain kali, ya?

cards.gloss_en: never mind; it's all right (standard; spoken: takpe / tak apa)
cards.gloss_ja: 大丈夫・かまわない（話し言葉は takpe / tak apa）
cards.note: Never mind; it's all right. The standard form. Everyday speech usually says «tak apa» or «takpe» (spoken).

cards.gloss_ja: そんなふうに（話し言葉）
cards.note: Spoken: «macam tu» for «seperti itu» (like that). Standard first: seperti itu (Ch15).
Spoken: «Set!» = Deal! Agreed! Standard first: setuju (above).
To treat someone, to pay for them: Bos belanja. belanja on its own is a root; you know berbelanja (Ch10) = to spend money, to shop.

cards.gloss_en: To drop in; to stop by
cards.note: To drop in, to stop by: Encik singgah di pejabat dulu, ya?
Spoken: «ni» for «ini» (this). Standard first: ini (Ch2).
Spoken: «tu» for «itu» (that). Standard first: itu (Ch2).
jemput (Dunia, Ch9) + -an: an invitation. Ini jemputan makan malam.

cards.gloss_en: never mind; it's OK (spoken short form of tak apa; standard tidak mengapa)
cards.gloss_ja: 大丈夫・かまわない（くだけた話し言葉、標準は tidak mengapa）
cards.note: Spoken: «takpe» is the short form of «tak apa» (never mind); both are everyday speech. The standard form is tidak mengapa (above). «tak apa» is also the Chapter 5 Dunia card. Recognise only.

cards.gloss_en: can't stand; can't handle (e.g. spicy food) (spoken: tak tahan)
cards.gloss_ja: 耐えられない、苦手だ（例：辛いもの）（話し言葉：tak tahan）
cards.note: Can't stand, can't handle (for example spicy food): Saya tidak boleh tahan pedas. The standard form; the spoken partner is «tak tahan» (below). It is not the same as «boleh tahan» (L-0939, Dunia, Ch5), which means «not bad»: a different expression.

cards.gloss_ja: 耐えられない、苦手だ（くだけた言い方）
cards.note: Spoken: «tak tahan» for «tidak boleh tahan» (can't stand, can't handle). Standard first: tidak boleh tahan (above). Everyday ways to say you don't want spicy food: Saya tak nak pedas. Saya tak suka pedas.
To reply. Sila balas sebelum hari Rabu.

frames.meaning_ja: いらっしゃいませんか。（丁寧な誘い方）

frames.frame: Sayangnya saya tidak ___. Lain kali, ya?
frames.example: Sayangnya saya tidak lapang. Lain kali, ya?
frames.meaning_en: Unfortunately I'm not free. Another time, then?
frames.meaning_ja: あいにく手が空いていません。また今度にしましょうか。
金曜日はいかがですか。
決まり！ 金曜日の7時ですね。（話し言葉：Set!）

frames.example: Tidak mengapa. Kita cuba lain kali.
frames.meaning_en: It's all right. We'll try another time. (Spoken: Takpe.)
frames.meaning_ja: 大丈夫ですよ。また今度やってみましょう。（話し言葉：Takpe.）

frames.meaning_en: Let's eat at this cafe! (Spoken: kat = di, ni = ini.)
frames.meaning_ja: このカフェで食べよう！（話し言葉：kat＝di、ni＝ini）

scenario.title_en: An invitation, and how people really talk
scenario.title_ja: お誘いと、ふだんの話し方

lines.speaker: Puan Aini
lines.ms: Encik Tanaka, ini jemputan makan malam pejabat. Hari Sabtu, pukul tujuh.
lines.en: Mr Tanaka, this is the invitation to the office dinner. Saturday at seven.

lines.speaker: Tanaka
lines.ms: Terima kasih, Puan Aini. Siapa yang belanja?
lines.en: Thank you, Puan Aini. Who is treating?

lines.speaker: Puan Aini
lines.ms: Bos belanja. Sudikah encik datang?
lines.en: The boss is treating. Would you like to come?

lines.speaker: Tanaka
lines.ms: Sayangnya hari Sabtu saya tidak lapang. Saya segan untuk menolak jemputan puan.
lines.en: Unfortunately I'm not free on Saturday. I'm reluctant to turn down your invitation, Puan.

lines.speaker: Puan Aini
lines.ms: Tidak mengapa. Ada cadangan lain?
lines.en: That's all right. Do you have another suggestion?

lines.speaker: Tanaka
lines.ms: Bagaimana kalau hari Jumaat?
lines.en: How about Friday?

lines.speaker: Puan Aini
lines.ms: Itu cadangan yang bagus. Saya tanya bos dulu.
lines.en: That's a good suggestion. I'll ask the boss first.

lines.speaker: Puan Aini
lines.ms: Bos setuju. Hari Jumaat, pukul tujuh. Encik singgah di pejabat dulu, ya? Kita pergi sama-sama.
lines.en: The boss agrees. Friday at seven. Drop by the office first, will you? We'll go together.

lines.speaker: Tanaka
lines.ms: Baik. Terima kasih!
lines.en: Fine. Thank you!

lines.speaker: Cik Mei Ling
lines.ms: Encik Tanaka, jom makan kat kafe ni! Saya belanja!
lines.en: Mr Tanaka, let's eat at this cafe! My treat!

lines.speaker: Tanaka
lines.ms: Terima kasih. Tetapi makanan di kafe itu pedas. Saya tidak boleh tahan pedas.
lines.en: But the food at that cafe is spicy. I can't stand spicy food.

lines.speaker: Cik Mei Ling
lines.ms: Takpelah. Kita cari kedai lain. Macam tu boleh?
lines.en: No problem. We'll look for another place. Would that be all right?

lines.speaker: Tanaka
lines.ms: Tadi cik cakap «takpe». Itu sama dengan «tidak mengapa», ya?
lines.en: You said «takpe» just now. That's the same as «tidak mengapa», right?

lines.speaker: Cik Mei Ling
lines.ms: Ya! Orang selalu cakap «tak apa» atau «takpe».
lines.en: Yes! People usually say «tak apa» or «takpe».

lines.speaker: Tanaka
lines.ms: Dan «lah» dan «kan»? Saya faham, tetapi saya tidak perlu cakap «lah», ya?
lines.en: And «lah» and «kan»? I understand them, but I don't have to say «lah», do I?

lines.speaker: Cik Mei Ling
lines.ms: Betul. Cakap seperti itu pun bagus, kan?
lines.en: Right. Speaking like that is fine too, isn't it?

lines.speaker: Tanaka
lines.ms: Ada kedai mamak dekat pejabat?
lines.en: Is there a mamak stall near the office?

lines.speaker: Cik Mei Ling
lines.ms: Ada, kedai mamak kat depan pejabat tu. Dekat sahaja.
lines.en: Yes, the mamak stall in front of the office. It's very close.

lines.speaker: Tanaka
lines.ms: Setuju! Mari kita pergi.
lines.en: Agreed! Let's go.

lines.speaker: Cik Mei Ling
lines.ms: Set!
lines.en: Deal!
